records.role_detail: denaturing it or modifying its conformation
records.mechanism_book_wording: They act on the stratum corneum intracellular keratin by denaturing it or modifying its conformation
records.quote: They act on the stratum corneum intracellular keratin by denaturing it or modifying its conformation, causing subsequent swelling and increased hydration
records.notes: BORDERLINE record; a later reader may want to drop it. 'They' = chemical percutaneous penetration enhancers as a class (section 2.2, lipid-protein-partitioning theory); no individual compound is tied to this statement. This is an excipient/formulation effect on a skin barrier protein, not a pharmacological drug-target mechanism. Classing keratin as a structural protein is my inference; the page does not use that term. The rule name 'Keratin Denaturant' is constructed from the book's verb 'denaturing'; the book does not print that phrase.

chapter_notes: The chapter is about skin-penetration enhancement (chemical enhancers, sonophoresis, iontophoresis, electroporation, microneedles, nanocarriers) and names no receptor or enzyme mechanism for any drug; the many drugs in Tables 2 and 4 are listed only as permeants, with no target stated. The single record is a borderline class-level statement about enhancers denaturing stratum corneum keratin; the same passage (PDF page 411) also says enhancers affect desmosomes and modify intercellular lipid domains / lipid bilayers, which were not recorded because no molecular target is named. Physical-method mechanisms (cavitation, electromigration, electroosmosis, pore formation) are not compound-target mechanisms and were not recorded.
